title: Knowledge check: Namespaces in XML Processing

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly covered in “Namespaces in XML Processing”?
questions.explanation: The attached XML curriculum lists “Namespace-aware parsers” under lesson 55, “Namespaces in XML Processing”. The other options are from different topics or unrelated areas.

questions.prompt: Which statement is the most reliable rule to remember when applying “Namespaces in XML Processing”?
options: A prefix is a local alias; expanded-name identity uses the namespace name and local name.
The text of the prefix is the namespace identity.
A default namespace automatically qualifies unprefixed attributes.
Two prefixes can never refer to the same namespace URI.
questions.answer_key: A prefix is a local alias; expanded-name identity uses the namespace name and local name.
questions.explanation: The correct choice separates the relevant XML concepts and avoids assumptions about processor behavior. Check the linked standard and actual implementation for details.

questions.prompt: After creating an example for “Namespaces in XML Processing”, what is the best next step?
options: Verify a normal case, an invalid or boundary case, and document the tool/version used.
Rely on visual appearance without parsing or validation.
Change several parts at once and infer the cause if the result changes.
questions.answer_key: Verify a normal case, an invalid or boundary case, and document the tool/version used.
questions.explanation: A small, reproducible test suite distinguishes expected behavior from a lucky example and makes version assumptions visible.
